parts.gloss: to those who do not guard

words.gloss: to those who do not guard

literal: Wealth possession to those who do not guard is not; compassion possession similarly is not to those who eat meat.
translation: The possession of wealth is not for those who fail to guard it; similarly, the possession of compassion is not for those who eat meat.
modern: பொருளைப் பாதுகாத்து வைக்காதவர்களுக்குச் செல்வம் சொந்தமாகாது; அதுபோலவே, மாமிசத்தை உண்பவர்களுக்கு அருளுடைமை சொந்தமாகாது.
explanation: This couplet draws a direct parallel between material wealth and spiritual compassion. Just as wealth slips away from those who do not actively protect and cherish it, the quality of compassion cannot exist in those who consume the flesh of animals. The word 'ஆட்சி' (possession or rule) is used in both halves to emphasize that neither wealth nor grace can be truly held without the right actions. Eating meat is presented as fundamentally incompatible with possessing a compassionate heart.
